login.title: Foundry Model Router console
login.lead: Sign in with your GitHub account. Once signed in you can create API keys and review your own calls and usage; administrators can also manage the routing strategy and the backend connections.

local.reveal: Sign in with a user name and password
local.hint: The local administrator account is for the case where github.com cannot be reached. It is configured in config.yaml and is not a GitHub account.
local.failed: That user name and password combination was not accepted.

blocked.title: GitHub OAuth must be configured first
blocked.lead: This service always verifies identity, but GitHub OAuth is not configured yet and the setup wizard only accepts requests from the machine running the service (127.0.0.1). Edit the auth.github section of config.yaml on the server, fill in client_id / client_secret and admin_logins, then restart the service.

setup.title: Setup: GitHub OAuth
setup.lead: First create an app under GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps, use the callback URL below, then paste the Client ID / Secret into this form. This wizard is only available while OAuth is unconfigured and you are on the local machine.
setup.secretPlaceholder: written to config.yaml (which is ignored by .gitignore)
setup.adminLoginsHint: separate several with commas or spaces
setup.save: Save configuration and go to sign-in
setup.localHint: Cannot reach github.com? Set auth.local_admin.enabled: true in config.yaml and sign in with the local administrator account (admin / admin1234). You will be required to change that password before anything else in the console becomes reachable.

password.title: Change the administrator password
password.lead: This account is still using the built-in default password, so nothing else in the console is reachable yet. Pick a new password to continue.
password.tooShort: The new password must be at least 8 characters.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
password.recovery: Locked out? Clear password_hash and password_salt under auth.local_admin in config.yaml and the built-in default password applies again.

created.title: Key created
created.note: Copy it into your client configuration now, or read it back at any time from the key list below — the key stays visible to you.
created.byokTitle: Use it in GitHub Copilot through BYOK
created.modelHint: any model name registered under Routing configuration
created.attribution: Every request made with this key is attributed to {{login}}, and the user_id in the trace is that GitHub account.

create.title: New key
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: something that tells the keys apart, e.g. copilot-laptop
create.blockedNote: Your account is not authorized to create keys, which also means you cannot use BYOK. The reason is under "Key creation permission" above.

admins.title: Administrators
admins.loginsHint: comma separated; effective as soon as you save
admins.note: Administrators see this page and Routing configuration, cross-user usage statistics and every trace, and are not subject to the enterprise key policy (otherwise a mistake in the policy would lock them out too). Emptying this list removes administrator rights from everybody, and the only way back is editing config.yaml.

signIn.title: Sign-in scope
signIn.allowAny: Allow any GitHub account to sign in
signIn.note: This switch governs signing in, not authorization. While it is on, any GitHub account can sign in and see its own (empty) data, but whether it may create an API key is decided by the key policy; while it is off, only the administrators listed above can sign in. Either way, calling /v1/chat/completions always requires a valid API key.

oauth.title: GitHub OAuth application
oauth.warning: Getting this wrong locks everybody out of signing in, including you, and the only way back is editing config.yaml on the server. Before changing anything, make sure the credentials come from GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps. Saving does not invalidate the current session, but the next sign-in uses the new credentials.
oauth.clientIdHint: the Client ID shown on the OAuth App page
oauth.clientSecretHint: visible only once when generated on GitHub; likewise never echoed back after being saved here
oauth.callbackUrlHint: leaving it empty is safest — it is derived from the request origin, honouring X-Forwarded-Proto / Host behind a reverse proxy
oauth.registerTitle: The URLs to register on GitHub
oauth.registerNote: These two fields in the OAuth App must match how this service is actually reached, or GitHub will reject the callback:

local.title: Local administrator
local.lead: A super administrator that signs in with a user name and password instead of GitHub, so the console stays reachable when github.com is not. It is always an administrator: it sees every user's traces and may delete them.
local.toggle: Allow signing in with the local administrator account
local.note: The credential lives in auth.local_admin in config.yaml, which is ignored by .gitignore, and only the salted hash is stored — never the password itself. Turning this off while GitHub OAuth is unconfigured leaves no way to sign in at all, and the only way back is editing config.yaml.
local.enabledSaved: Local administrator sign-in is now enabled
local.disabledSaved: Local administrator sign-in is now disabled
local.passwordSaved: Saved: the new credential is in force and every other local-administrator session was signed out
local.neverChanged: still on the built-in default password
local.usernameHint: changing it signs out the other sessions of this account
local.currentHint: the built-in default while none has been set
local.nextHint: at least 8 characters, and not the built-in default
local.recovery: Locked out? Clear password_hash and password_salt under auth.local_admin in config.yaml: the built-in default password applies again, and the console will require you to change it on the next sign-in.

cache.title: Local GitHub cache
cache.refreshed: Refreshed from GitHub and written to data/github
cache.lead: The enterprise / organization / team structure and their member lists are kept in data/github and refreshed on a timer, so a membership check is a local set lookup rather than a GitHub round trip. A scope whose member list is truncated or errored is never treated as authoritative — those checks fall back to a live probe, because "not in the part of the list I could read" is not "not a member".
cache.intervalHint: at least 60; applies after you save this page
cache.unavailable: Nothing has been cached yet. Save an Enterprise token and refresh.

policy.title: Key creation policy
policy.toggle: Only allow users in the listed enterprises / organizations to create API keys
policy.enabledNote: Enabled: when a standard user creates a key, their enterprise and organization membership is checked against GitHub live, and a user who belongs to no allowed scope is rejected (403) and therefore cannot use BYOK. Administrators are exempt.
policy.disabledNote: Not enabled: any GitHub account that can sign in can create an API key and use BYOK. If "Allow any GitHub account to sign in" above is also on, that means the whole of GitHub.
policy.missingTokenNote: The policy is enabled but no Enterprise token is configured, so the service cannot verify membership and currently rejects every key creation request from a non-administrator. Fill in the token below.
policy.tokenUnsaved: The token has been changed but is not saved yet. Only a saved token can be used to fetch the enterprise list automatically.
policy.needTokenFirst: Fill in and save the Enterprise token first, and the enterprises visible to it will be listed here.
policy.fetchingFromGitHub: Fetching the enterprise list from GitHub…
policy.noEnterprises: No enterprises are visible to this token.
policy.noEnterprisesVisible: No enterprises are visible to this token. Make sure it has the admin:enterprise scope.
policy.structureLead: The structure below comes straight from the GitHub API. Turn on the master switch for an enterprise, then choose which organizations or enterprise teams may create API keys.
policy.nobodyAllowed: The policy is enabled but no enterprise is allowed — right now nobody except administrators can create an API key.
policy.entOffNote: The master switch is off — the organization and team settings for this enterprise have no effect at all.
policy.allowAllOrgs: Let members of any organization in this enterprise create keys
policy.allOrgsNote: With this on you do not have to tick organizations one by one. The order of evaluation is: direct enterprise membership first, then each listed organization is probed in turn (up to 30).
policy.allOrgsTruncated: This enterprise has {{total}} organizations and only the first {{listed}} are listed; the ones not listed will not be probed — turn this off and tick them individually if you need exact control.
policy.allOrgsOffNote: While it is off, only the organizations and enterprise teams ticked below count.
policy.orgsListedPartially: {{total}} organizations in total; only the first {{listed}} are listed here.
policy.allowedTeamsHint: membership is decided by the team's numeric id (GitHub accepts nothing else); the team name is what is shown here and to users
policy.teamListUnavailableNote: — this enterprise can only be authorized by organization.
policy.noTeams: This enterprise has no enterprise teams.

providers.title: Backend connections (providers)
providers.lead: A connection is one "address + key" pair. Models inherit the connection marked "default", or bind to one of their own — which can be Azure AI Foundry in a different environment, or any OpenAI-compatible service. Keys are stored in config.yaml on the server (that file is ignored by .gitignore).
providers.empty: No connections yet. Add one before binding models to it.
providers.promptName: Name of the new connection (models reference it by this name, e.g. openrouter):
providers.stillReferenced: The connection "{{name}}" is still referenced by the model(s) {{models}} — rebind them under Model catalog first
providers.isDefaultConnection: The connection "{{name}}" is the default connection — point the default at another connection first
providers.baseUrlHint: for Azure use https://xxx.openai.azure.com/; for OpenAI-compatible go all the way to /v1
providers.apiKeyPlaceholder: leave empty to fall back to AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY from .env

models.title: Model catalog
models.lead: The names here are the model names a client may send in a request. The descriptions are handed to the AI decision model as the candidate catalog, so spelling out "what kind of task this suits" improves routing accuracy noticeably. Connections are maintained under <providersLink>Backend connections</providersLink>.
models.empty: No models yet. Add at least one and mark it as the default model.
models.promptName: The name this new model is exposed under in the router:
models.removedWithRules_one: Deleted the model "{{name}}" along with {{count}} rule that referenced it
models.removedWithRules_other: Deleted the model "{{name}}" along with {{count}} rules that referenced it
models.descriptionHint: read by the AI decision model
models.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g.: flagship high-end model. Suits the hardest reasoning, large system design and gnarly bug analysis.
models.modelNameOverrideHint: leave empty to use the model name above
models.isDefault: Default model (used when no rule matches or the decision fails)

ai.title: AI routing
ai.desc: A lightweight decision model reads the request's intent and picks a model. Accurate, at the cost of one extra ~1s decision call per request.

rule.title: Rule routing
rule.desc: Matched in order by keyword and prompt length. Zero LLM calls, under 1ms, and the rules are maintained under <rulesLink>Rule routing</rulesLink>.

session.title: Session stickiness
session.sticky: Pin one model per session (better consistency and cache hit rate)
session.stickyNote: With this on, the model chosen for a user interaction is reused for the rest of it: an agentic client's tool-call loop keeps one model and pays for one routing decision. Requests are grouped by the x-interaction-id header that clients such as GitHub Copilot already send, and by x-session-id when one is supplied.
session.ttlHint: how long an idle session keeps its binding

aiRouter.title: AI decision model
aiRouter.inactive: the strategy is currently rule routing, so the settings below have no effect
aiRouter.decisionModelHint: pick a light, fast one, e.g. gpt-4.1
aiRouter.decisionProvider: Connection used by the decision model
aiRouter.timeoutHint: a timeout falls back to the default model
aiRouter.maxPromptCharsHint: beyond this, half is kept from each end

rules.title: Rule routing
rules.inactive: the strategy is currently AI routing, so rules have no effect
rules.lead: Evaluated top to bottom; the first rule that matches decides the model and the rest are skipped — use ↑↓ to reorder. If nothing matches, the default model {{model}} is used. When one rule carries both keywords and a length, only the length is checked. The strategy switch lives under Routing strategy.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Under the rule routing strategy, every request goes to the default model.
rules.keywordsHint: comma separated, case insensitive, any one match routes

prompt.title: AI decision prompt
prompt.lead: This is the system content sent to the decision model. {{placeholder}} is replaced with the name and description of every model on the Model catalog page. Leave it empty to use the built-in default. Keep the instruction that the decision model must output only {{shape}} — a response that cannot be parsed silently falls back to the default model.
prompt.templateHint: empty = built-in default; braces need no escaping
prompt.noPlaceholderWarning: The template has no {{placeholder}}: the model catalog is appended at the end automatically (see the preview below), but you do not control where. Inserting the placeholder explicitly is recommended.
prompt.missingDescription_one: {{count}} model has no description: {{models}} — it is just a name in the catalog, so the decision model can hardly tell whether to pick it.
prompt.missingDescription_other: {{count}} models have no description: {{models}} — they are just names in the catalog, so the decision model can hardly tell whether to pick them.
prompt.previewHint: rendered by the backend from the current draft, by the same code a real request uses
prompt.sampleHint: type a user question to preview what the user message looks like after truncation
prompt.samplePlaceholder: e.g.: help me refactor this module's architecture
prompt.sampleTruncated: truncated to {{count}} characters, half from each end
prompt.defaultLoaded: The built-in default prompt has been loaded into the editor; keep editing if you like, and save to apply
